sources.entry: OpenVoiceFlow - On-device voice dictation for macOS with local transcription and optional text cleanup.

summary.one_liner: OpenVoiceFlow is a free, open-source macOS dictation app that transcribes speech on-device with WhisperKit, so you hold a key, talk, and release to paste text into any app.
keywords: open source alternative to paid dictation apps
summary.what_it_does: OpenVoiceFlow runs as a menu bar app on macOS. You hold a push-to-talk key (default fn), speak, and release, and the transcribed text is pasted at the cursor via a simulated Cmd+V with clipboard restore. Transcription uses WhisperKit running Whisper models locally, from tiny (39 MB) to large-v3-turbo, and live partial text appears in a floating HUD while you speak. An optional AI cleanup step, off by default, can polish grammar and filler words through OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, or a local Ollama model, with API keys stored in the macOS Keychain and only text (never audio) sent to those services. It also includes a personal dictionary, spoken snippets that expand to longer text, and per-app writing styles, plus a dashboard for history and stats. Updates are delivered via Sparkle.
use_cases: dictate emails and documents by voice on a Mac
speak text into any app instead of typing
private offline transcription without cloud uploads
cleaning up dictated text grammar and filler words
teaching a dictation tool names and technical jargon
replacing a paid subscription voice typing app
how_to_run: Download the DMG from the project's download page, drag it to Applications, and open it (signed and notarized, universal build)
git clone the repository and cd into openvoiceflow
Install XcodeGen: brew install xcodegen (requires macOS 14+ and Xcode 16.4+)
Run: bash native/scripts/run-local.sh (generates the Xcode project, builds an ad-hoc-signed debug app, and launches it)
notable: Audio is processed in memory on-device and nothing is recorded while the key is not held
Optional AI cleanup supports five backends including fully local Ollama
Ad-hoc signing for debug builds is explained because macOS ties Accessibility and Input Monitoring grants to code signatures
Anonymous aggregate usage sharing is on by default with a single switch to disable; dictation text is never included
Legacy Python app retained for macOS 12-13 fallback builds
caveats: Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer; macOS 12-13 only get a retained legacy build
Legacy Python app (voiceflow/, version 0.3.6 and below) is end-of-life with no security fixes
Anonymous aggregate usage sharing is enabled by default (can be switched off)
Building from source requires Xcode 16.4+ and XcodeGen
